yt_posts.topic: Kaspa Dollar: a KAS-backed stablecoin proposal with a miner-voted oracle and no admin key, and Mike's question (why not just USDT and USDC?)
yt_posts.body_style: open question, then how it works, the timeline, the debate, the comment ask
yt_posts.body:
Kaspa is getting its own dollar. Not USDT. Not USDC. A stablecoin minted against locked KAS, priced by the miners themselves, with no admin key anywhere in the design. And my first reaction when I saw it was a question I still haven't fully answered.

First, what it is. Kaspa Dollar is an initiative led by a Kaspa core developer to build the first decentralized, overcollateralized stablecoin on Kaspa. The whitepaper landed in early November, and the ticker people are using for it, KSD, is still a working label.

Here's how it works. You lock $KAS in a vault and mint dollars against it. KAS is the only collateral, and every dollar is backed by more than a dollar of it. This only became possible this year, when covenants went live on Kaspa with the Toccata hard fork on June 30.

Now the part I find really interesting: the oracle. There's no outside price feed. Kaspa miners vote the KAS price right inside the blocks they mine, and the protocol takes the median. Miner-voted oracles. The same proof of work that secures the chain prices the dollar.

It's early, though. This is a working draft with audits still ahead. Testnet is planned for May 2027 and mainnet is targeted for September 2027, and those are development targets that can move. One more thing so nobody gets confused: $KDOLLAR is a community meme coin raising funds for the project. It is not the stablecoin, and holding it doesn't give you a dollar peg.

So here's my question. If you want a stablecoin on Kaspa, why not just bring USDT and USDC over? When you deviate from what the whole market already uses, you want a damn good reason, because otherwise it comes across as weird and fewer people adopt it.

The answer I keep hearing: USDT and USDC have an issuer who can freeze them, and a dollar with no admin key doesn't. I get that argument. I'm still working through whether it's enough.

So tell me: does Kaspa need its own decentralized dollar, or should it just bring USDT and USDC over? Drop a comment and tell me what I'm missing.

If this helped you make sense of Kaspa Dollar, hit like and subscribe so you catch the next one.

yt_posts.topic: Bitcoin's 12.6% week and the close under its 200-week SMA: the midterms, the Anthropic IPO, why it's both, and what the economy actually needs
yt_posts.body_style: stat shock, two theories, the precedent, the synthesis, the macro line, the comment ask
yt_posts.body:
Bitcoin lost 12.6% in the week of November 9 and closed below its 200-week SMA. Half the timeline says it's the midterms. The other half says it's the Anthropic IPO. Here's my revolutionary thought: what if it's just both?

The numbers first. Bitcoin opened that week near $74.8K and closed near $65.3K, with a low under $62K. The 200-week SMA sits around $68K. That's the fourth weekly close under that line this year.

Theory one is the midterms. On November 5 the S&P 500 had its biggest one-day dollar drop ever, on fear of an AI crackdown after the elections, and risk came off everywhere. That's one cause for a dump.

Theory two is the IPO. Anthropic is slated to list on Nasdaq on November 19, selling 825 million shares at $70 to $78. That's up to around $64 billion that has to come from somewhere, and the theory is that some of it comes out of Bitcoin. This is relatively new for crypto: smart money pulling a million dollars out of Bitcoin to buy into the hot new listing. Then you get the people who say, I know they're going to sell, so I'm selling first.

There's a precedent. SpaceX listed on June 12, the largest IPO ever, and Bitcoin printed its low of the year near $57.7K less than three weeks later.

So put the two together. One reason to dump, one reason to raise cash, and a crowd front-running both. That's how you get candles like these.

Here's what isn't broken: the economy. The ISM PMI came in at 55.5 for October, the tenth straight month of expansion. It's just not explosive yet. And we don't need QE to get there. We need rates to come down so loans get plentiful, businesses spend, new jobs get created, and people with paychecks go buy crypto.

What do I expect? I doubt we get a giant green candle right away. Another few weeks of this wouldn't surprise me. If Bitcoin holds above that summer low, there's no new bottom. Meanwhile the four-year cycle zombies moved their bottom from October to November. I've been buying a bunch of plays at really low prices, and I don't touch leverage.

So what do you think is really behind this dump: the midterms, the Anthropic IPO, or both? Tell me in the comments.

If this gave you a clearer read on the selloff, hit like and subscribe for more macro and crypto without the four-year cycle noise.
